The United States of America is the federal republic that grew from thirteen British colonies on the Atlantic coast of North America. The map shows it under this name in 1783, 1800, 1880 and 1900, which tracks its growth across the continent. The main page for the country is United States.

  • 1783: the Treaty of Paris ended the war of independence and set the western border at the Mississippi River.
  • 1800: the young republic ran under the Constitution of 1787, with sixteen states. The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 soon doubled its size.
  • 1880: it reached the Pacific after the Mexican-American War and had survived the Civil War, which ended slavery. Native nations had been pushed west, as on the Trail of Tears, and onto reservations.
  • 1900: it had become an industrial giant and an overseas power, taking Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines in the Spanish-American War of 1898 and annexing Hawaii.
